item.title: Rooftop terraces lift Beijing urban renewal to new heights
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-14
BEIJING, Sept. 14 (Xinhua) -- "If you think you've seen Beijing, you haven't been here yet," Elizaveta, a Russian woman who has lived in China for seven years, wrote on her social media account. The "here" she refers to is a rooftop terrace atop a commercial building on the site of the original Longfu Temple, a 15th-century Buddhist landmark. Now part of a vibrant cultural hub, the terrace offers one of Beijing's most compelling vantage points, where history and modernity meet beneath the skyline. To the east, Beijing's glass-and-steel skyline rises against the horizon. To the west lies the older city, with the glazed roofs of the Palace Museum glistening, the forested slopes of Jingshan Hill stretching and the white pagoda of Beihai Park standing gracefully in the distance. "For a moment," Elizaveta wrote, "I really feel like I'm standing at the edge of two eras." The terrace reflects a broader citywide shift. Earlier this year, Beijing issued a plan for high-quality urban development, vowing to make better use of historic streets and industrial heritage, upgrade key commercial districts, and create new consumption scenarios. The initiative is part of a national drive to turn 1,500 old neighborhoods and industrial districts into new engines of consumption and culture by 2030. Subject to building height limits, Beijing's central areas preserve a low skyline defined by iconic imperial red walls, yellow-tiled roofs and traditional alleys, where residents still live amid dense greenery. These open vistas offer visitors ample opportunities to appreciate the city's distinctive architectural heritage. Amid urban renewal efforts, Beijing's Dongcheng district, home to many of the capital's most treasured historic sites and blocks of siheyuan, or quadrangle courtyards, launched in 2025 a "Breeze Terrace" initiative to turn idle rooftops into public gathering spaces. Government, residents and merchants have worked together to bring in viewing decks, reading corners, dining spaces and craft workshops. According to planners, the idea is to let people see the city from a different angle without major demolition or construction. Since its launch, the initiative has drawn more than 1 million visits. This summer, it added about 300 terraces across the district, linked by four themed routes covering Central Axis vistas, hutong discoveries, literary corners and night tours. Chen Shiqi, an influencer who scouts shops and restaurants for his followers, called terraces "one of the surest ways to go viral" on Chinese social media. Comparing his own posts on Xiaohongshu, a popular Chinese lifestyle-sharing app, he found that using terrace photos as cover images consistently draws more readers. Over the past year, about 30 to 40 percent of the spots Chen has reviewed have been rooftop venues. Sometimes when he doesn't name the location, followers message him privately to ask where it is. Chen's observation points to a broader trend of the social media era. Visitors no longer simply experience a view. They photograph and share it, and rooftop terraces, with their sweeping backdrops and curated aesthetics, serve that purpose perfectly. Yet all of this would be unthinkable without the blue skies above. Beijing's anti-pollution campaign, launched in 2013, has cut the annual average of PM2.5, the fine particles linked to respiratory disease, from 89.5 micrograms per cubic meter to 27 last year, a sharp drop of nearly 70 percent. "Beijing blue," once a novelty worth a social media post, has become the background of daily life. In addition, Beijing's temperate climate and relatively low rainfall provide more clear-sky days for rooftop outings than many other major Chinese cities -- Shanghai included -- giving the city a natural edge for its growing terrace economy. On a rooftop garden of the Jinbao Place shopping mall, visitors can join sunset yoga, pick herbs, attend moonlit cocktail parties, try on Hanfu, or even hold a wedding. The once-forgotten space has become a vibrant consumer destination. "Rooftop terraces, as a key setting for urban renewal, hold great potential to nurture new consumption, improve public spaces and revitalize the old city's cultural heritage," said Xing Yan, deputy chief planner at the Beijing Tsinghua Tongheng urban planning and design institute. The next step, Xing added, is to extend Beijing's urban renewal efforts across the ground level, building facades, and rooftops, unlocking greater value from the city's existing space. The growing appeal of these rooftop spaces makes them a must-visit for Chen and his photography-obsessed friends. "The only problem," Chen said with a laugh, "is that my friends are so obsessed with getting the perfect shot that they can easily spend an hour taking photos." "Sometimes the food gets cold, and we have to ask the waiter to reheat it!" ■

item.title: Pickleball in China: How a tiny ball is driving a big industry
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-14
Pickleball, a sport originating in the United States and combining elements of tennis, badminton and table tennis, is gaining popularity across China, bringing new opportunities to cities and creating another platform for sporting exchanges between China and the rest of the world. ZHENGZHOU, Sept. 14 (Xinhua) -- The 2026 China National Pickleball Championships was held in early September in Hebi, central China's Henan Province, drawing more than 30 teams from across the country. Preliminary statistics show that pickleball, once a niche sport, has been included as a mass-participation event in the games of 10 provincial-level regions this year, including Henan, Guangxi and Beijing. The China Pickleball Circuit, which had just over 80 stops when it launched in 2024, has expanded to 1,000 stops this year. Originating in the United States and combining elements of tennis, badminton and table tennis, pickleball is rapidly gaining popularity across China. The sport is bringing new opportunities to cities and creating another platform for sporting exchanges between China and the rest of the world. A CITY TRANSFORMED BY A BALL Every morning, the sharp crack of pickleballs echoes along the banks of the Qi River in Hebi. Zhang Shaohua, a Hebi resident born in the 1970s, has been hooked on pickleball since she first tried it in 2024. To promote the sport more widely, she set up a players' community and built her own professional pickleball venue. She also travels regularly around the country to play and connect with other enthusiasts. "In Hebi, pickleball started as a trend, but it has become a daily routine," Zhang said. In just three years, the once-obscure sport has taken off in Hebi. "Hebi has a solid industrial foundation and rich cultural and tourism resources, but its urban visibility and influence still need to be enhanced. We urgently need to build a highly recognizable city brand that can connect with both domestic and international markets," said Zhao Hongyu, secretary of the CPC Hebi Municipal Committee. By 2025, the city had built 1,600 pickleball courts, giving it one of the highest densities of pickleball courts in China and forming a network covering urban areas, counties and townships. Pickleball has not only raised Hebi's profile, but also helped spur the development of related industries. Leveraging its existing coal chemical, rubber and plastics industries, Hebi has built a pickleball industrial chain that spans from raw materials such as polypropylene to the production of high-end equipment. At a factory in Xun County, Hebi, machines hum as pickleball paddles, nets and sports flooring roll off the production line. The company, which started as a rubber and plastic products manufacturer, began making pickleball equipment in 2024. Its pickleball equipment sales exceeded 25 million yuan in 2025, up more than 50 percent year on year, and are projected to top 50 million yuan in 2026. "We export pickleball-related products to Europe, the Americas and Southeast Asia," said Xing Weimin, general manager of Henan Geli Sports Goods Co., Ltd. "Recently, customers have come to the factory almost every day to discuss business. The pickleball market has huge potential." A SPORT SPREADING WIDELY IN CHINA In 2026, pickleball is surging across China with unprecedented momentum, sweeping through cities large and small and drawing participants from schoolchildren to retirees alike. "There are currently eight million people in China who regularly participate in pickleball, and about 20 million who have tried it," said Bai Xilin, director of the Tennis Administration Center of China's General Administration of Sport. "The number of active pickleball players in China may reach 30 million in the future." Beyond Hebi, cities across China are exploring creative ways to weave pickleball into urban life. Hangzhou's Gongshu District has turned unused space beneath an elevated highway into a 6,000-square-meter pickleball park with five standard courts. Beijing's Fengtai District has converted a former indoor basketball arena into a pickleball club that now hosts the Beijing Pickleball Super League. Suzhou, Jiangsu Province, has opened a 23-court complex, the largest in the province, which offered four hours of play for just 29.9 yuan during the summer, drawing scores of young players. Nanjing has 11 standard courts on the 51st floor of a shopping mall, offering panoramic city views. Hosting pickleball tournaments has also emerged as a new way to blend culture, sports, tourism and commerce while stimulating local consumption. "I believe that pickleball has the potential to become the next marathon-like popular sport," said Song Hongfei, general manager of the sports business division at Viva Goods Co., Ltd. According to the China Sporting Goods Federation, China's domestic market for pickleball equipment and services exceeded 1.8 billion yuan in 2025 and is projected to grow at a compound annual rate of 47 percent over the next five years. Enthusiasm for hosting tournaments is also surging. In just over two years, China Pickleball Circuit events alone have been staged in 99 cities across more than 20 provincial-level regions, while grassroots tournaments have proliferated as well. "Many cities host marathons, which not only promote national fitness but also play an important role in enhancing the city's brand, and pickleball is developing in the same direction," said Qiao Liang of Henan Dongcheng Sports Industry Co., Ltd. MORE THAN JUST A GAME Bai Xilin described pickleball's broad appeal as "three lows and three highs." The "three lows" start with a low barrier to entry: men and women, young and old, and even complete beginners can pick it up quickly. Second is low cost-courts are flexible and equipment is relatively inexpensive. Third is low risk: as a non-contact sport, it suits a wide range of ages. The "three highs" are its strong social dimension, high overall value and high safety rating. Its overall value encompasses fitness, social, economic and cultural benefits. Pickleball has also seen rapid international growth in recent years. According to 2026 statistics from a sports and fitness industry association in the United States, where the sport originated, pickleball has been the fastest-growing sport in the country for five consecutive years. In Southeast Asia, including Vietnam and the Philippines, it has also built a broad participation base. In 2025, the Hebi International Pickleball Invitational brought together professional players from 14 countries and regions, including Spain, Italy and Sweden, to compete alongside Chinese athletes and exchange skills. In February and August this year, two groups of American teachers and students visited Hebi. They paired up with local teenagers for friendly matches and shared pickleball skills. They also visited an ancient temple fair, experienced a molten-iron fireworks display and made traditional clay whistles known as "Nigugu," gaining deeper insight into Chinese culture. Through friendly matches and cultural exchanges, pickleball is creating lasting bonds that transcend borders and bring people closer together. ■

item.title: In Yan'an, visitors see how CPC turns history into progress
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-14
YAN'AN, Shaanxi, Sept. 14 (Xinhua) -- When Ivan Racan was still a boy, not yet 10 years old, his father returned to Croatia from China in 1981, carrying with him a sanxian -- a traditional three-stringed Chinese instrument. The instrument hung on the wall of his childhood room, bringing a piece of distant China into his everyday life. More than 40 years later, Racan came across a similar instrument at a museum in Shanghai. He was struck by the realization that while the sanxian had remained much the same, China itself had transformed dramatically. For Racan, a member of the Croatian Parliament and son of former Croatian Prime Minister Ivica Racan, the instrument connects two periods of China's modern history. His father had visited China as an official of the former Yugoslavia. When he returned, he brought back stories that captured the early days of a transformation, one that would go on to reshape the country over the decades to come, Racan said. Decades later, Racan visited China himself and made a point to travel to Yan'an, which was once a center of the Chinese revolution. During his journey through the city in northwest China's Shaanxi Province, he encountered a modern country that would have been difficult to imagine in 1981. On Sept. 10, more than 200 representatives from over 50 countries attended a thematic briefing in Yan'an. Through stories of rural development, ecological conservation, industrial upgrading and cultural heritage protection, the event demonstrated how the Communist Party of China (CPC) has translated long-term goals into changes that reach communities and ordinary families. "This is something that has to be commended, appreciated, studied," Racan told Xinhua. For Petre Danci, a parliamentary advisor at the Office of the Secretary of the Romanian Senate and secretary of the Romania-China Friendship Group within the Alliance for the Union of Romanians, China's transformation is not an inherited memory. It is part of his own life. Danci, who speaks fluent Mandarin, arrived in Beijing in 2011. He studied Chinese at the Capital University of Economics and Business before completing bachelor's and master's degrees. During seven years of study and life in Beijing, he experienced China through lectures, friendships and the everyday norms of student life. "Every single time I come to China, I see a lot of development," he said. "Even if I go to a very familiar city, like Beijing, or Shanghai, or some other big cities, I still see the improvement." His latest journey to Yan'an brought him face to face with an earlier chapter of China's history. Danci learned about the period when Yan'an served as a center of the Chinese revolution and said he could still feel the Yan'an spirit in China today. That connection became clearer when he heard about the development of Liangjiahe Village, the technological upgrading of traditional industries and the restoration of environmentally fragile land through years of afforestation. "It takes function, leadership and organization," Danci told Xinhua. He believed China's experience in agriculture, ecological restoration and industrial modernization could offer useful references for Romania. Such experience should not be copied mechanically, he said, but adapted to local conditions through exchanges among people, businesses and governments. Having studied the Chinese language and experienced the country as a student, Danci said he hoped to help strengthen communication between Romania and China. The connection between Yan'an's revolutionary history and China's present-day development was expressed most directly by Leevameng Leebouapao, deputy director general of the Land Department at the Ministry of Natural Resources and Environment of Laos. During a visit to Nangou Village in Yan'an, he saw how poverty alleviation, public infrastructure and improvements to the rural environment had changed people's lives. "Socialism creates conditions for equality," he said. "People have equal access to education, healthcare, transport and other public services. China has demonstrated this in practice." What impressed him was that development had not been limited to major cities such as Beijing and Shanghai. Roads, communications networks and public services had also reached rural communities. In Nangou Village, he said, the practical work of the CPC and the government had made life more convenient for villagers and significantly improved their living environment. He added that China's experience in poverty alleviation and improving people's livelihoods deserved to be studied by other developing countries, including Laos. Beneath Pagoda Hill in Yan'an, visitors did not simply listen to stories about the CPC's past, but also to how the spirit formed in Yan'an continues to shape China's development today. ■

item.title: AI moves from elite competition to everyday sports in China
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-14
Fitness enthusiasts are increasingly gaining access to AI-powered technologies in everyday sports, driving the digital upgrade of China's sports sector. by sportswriter Li Chunyu BEIJING, Sept. 14 (Xinhua) -- While sports fans have become accustomed to AI-assisted officiating at major events such as the FIFA World Cup and Grand Slam tennis tournaments, fitness enthusiasts are increasingly gaining access to similar technology in everyday sports. At the 2026 China International Fair for Trade in Services, held at Beijing's Shougang Park this week, organizers transformed the sports services exhibition area into a functioning sports venue to showcase how artificial intelligence is being applied to training, officiating and fitness. On an indoor tennis court, visitors waited to try an AI-powered system that tracks player movement, ball trajectories, landing positions and shot speed. "On-site cameras capture live footage of every rally. Whether in training or competition, this intelligent agent generates in-depth performance analytics and highlight videos based on the data," said Gao Kai, a product operations manager for the Smartshot system. "This smart system is redefining how players train, compete and refine their games. It has already been deployed across cities in China, including Beijing, Guangzhou, Shenyang and Yinchuan. The technology has also been gradually introduced in Canada, Australia and other markets," Gao added. The exhibition area also featured a simulated video assistant referee control room for football developed by Beijing Rigour Technology, alongside intelligent officiating systems for volleyball, baseball and softball. In 2023, FIFA confirmed that Rigour's VAR and offside technologies had been tested and certified to FIFA standards. "Human referees are limited by eyesight and reaction time, making it difficult to capture every detail in fast-paced competitions. The intelligent system offers an objective replay," said Wu Guoyu, a project manager with Rigour Technology. For football offside decisions, for example, the system analyzes camera feeds using deep-learning AI models and image-processing algorithms. Once an offside is detected, it generates a precise offside line on the broadcast feed to assist referees. While such technology is used in elite competitions, developers are also introducing it to grassroots and youth sports. "Many amateur tournaments lack professional referees and may simply rely on trust, which means calls over whether a ball is in or out are left to the players to agree on. That often leads to disputes," Wu said. "A more accessible intelligent officiating system is much needed for the public." AI and digital technology are also expanding the possibilities for recreational fitness. Sports such as rowing and canoeing traditionally require access to water, while skiing requires snow and specialized facilities. Virtual sports can simulate those activities in a wider range of locations. "Virtual sports venues can serve as daily fitness hubs while also hosting virtual sports events to inject vitality into people's lives," exhibitor Mei Zijia said. "Sports services are no longer merely about selling goods, but providing a set of solutions tailored to different sporting scenarios." A report on China's sports services trade and development released during CIFTIS showed that the country's total imports and exports of major sports services reached 74.875 billion yuan (11.16 billion U.S. dollars) in 2025, up 7.98 percent year on year. "China's sports services trade has reached new heights, with significant improvements in its trade structure and sports economy," said Yang Xuedong, economic director at China's General Administration of Sport. "We will accelerate the adoption of big data and artificial intelligence to empower the sports industry through technological innovation." ■

item.title: Fear-mongering will only disrupt process of global AI governance: spokesperson
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-14
BEIJING, Sept. 14 (Xinhua) -- Fear-mongering, confrontation and vicious competition will only disrupt the process of global AI governance, which serves no one's interest, a Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson said on Monday. Spokesperson Guo Jiakun made the remarks after some top lab CEOs called for slowing the technology's development. "The development of AI bears on the well-being of all humanity. All parties should jointly promote the open and inclusive development of AI for good and for all," Guo told a regular press briefing. According to media reports, Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei on Saturday called on AI companies to slow the rate at which they advance model capabilities amid mounting fears of misuse of artificial intelligence. Both Elon Musk, who runs xAI, and Sam Altman, CEO of OpenAI, said that they agree with Amodei. ■

item.title: China to create more friendly environment for childbearing with better childcare services
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-14
The State Council Information Office holds a press conference on making decisive progress in the Healthy China initiative in Beijing, capital of China, Sept. 14, 2026. (Xinhua/Zhang Yuwei) BEIJING, Sept. 14 (Xinhua) -- China will take further steps to support childbearing, including making childcare more accessible and affordable, a senior health official announced Monday, as the country seeks to ease costs of raising children and boost its birth rate. Lei Haichao, head of the National Health Commission, told a media conference that continuous efforts will be made to promote the integrated development of services at kindergartens and nursery centers and to support communities and employers in setting up childcare facilities. The aim is to ensure that families can access childcare services close to their homes or workplaces and at relatively affordable prices, Lei said. The commission will work to raise coverage of childcare services among young children to effectively reduce families' costs of having, raising and educating children, the official said. The country will also work to improve access to pediatric care at grassroots medical institutions, according to Lei. By the end of this year, 1,000 more community-level medical and health institutions will be capable of offering pediatric care compared with last year, Lei said, adding that by that time, more than 95 percent of the country's township-level clinics and community health service centers are expected to have the capacity to provide relevant services. Over 3,000 pediatricians have been sent from higher-level hospitals to grassroots medical institutions to strengthen pediatric services at the community level, Lei said. China has developed a full-cycle maternity support system covering pre-pregnancy, pregnancy and childbirth, and child-rearing, with measures that include maternity allowances, childcare subsidies, medical insurance reimbursement and affordable childcare services to ease the financial burden on families with children. The country introduced a nationwide childcare subsidy program in 2025, offering an annual tax-free subsidy of 3,600 yuan (about 530 U.S. dollars) for each child under the age of three. It also began waiving childcare and education fees for the final year of kindergarten in the 2025 autumn semester. As of August, more than 25 million infants and toddlers have received childcare subsidies for 2026, and about 24 million children enrolled in kindergartens have benefited from the fee-waiving policy. Also, 260 million people are currently covered by maternity insurance, and many regions are expanding coverage to allow flexible workers to enroll in maternity insurance alongside employee medical insurance. These policies are among China's broader efforts to build a birth-friendly society amid declining birth rates and an aging population. Building a "birth-friendly society" has become a key focus of China's 15th Five-Year Plan. The outline sets out measures, including incentives to encourage births and efforts to reduce the costs of childbirth, childcare and education. It says the goal is to stabilize the number of newborns and support long-term balanced population development. ■

item.title: Xi charts course for high-quality development of greater BRICS cooperation, Chinese FM says
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-14
BEIJING, Sept. 13 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping's attendance at the BRICS summit in India is of strategic significance for steering the high-quality development for greater BRICS cooperation, Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi said Sunday. The South Asian trip also promoted strength through unity among Global South countries, Wang said. Wang, also a member of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China Central Committee, made the remarks while briefing reporters on Xi's visit to India to attend the 18th BRICS Summit on Saturday and Sunday. First, Xi's visit injected fresh impetus into BRICS cooperation. The Chinese president summed up the development of BRICS over the past two decades with three key phrases: self-reliance and self-strengthening, standing together through wind and rain, and fruitful outcomes, Wang said. Standing at a new historical starting point, Xi called on BRICS countries to be pioneers in advancing innovation-driven development, upholding peace and stability, facilitating mutual learning between civilizations, and reforming and improving global governance, Wang said. In 2027, the BRICS will usher in its fourth "China Year." Xi announced that China will take this opportunity to work with all parties to build consensus, open up prospects for the future, and embark on the third golden decade of BRICS cooperation, Wang said. Second, Xi's visit empowered the Global South, Wang said. Xi put forward four important proposals to strengthen the Global South: jointly defending the rule of law in international affairs and ensuring that international law and international rules are applied to all; holding high the banner of multilateralism and upholding the authority and role of the United Nations; staying committed to a people-centered development philosophy and striving to deliver on the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development; and jointly advancing security governance and tackling both traditional and nontraditional security threats, Wang said. Focusing on the new round of scientific and technological revolution and industrial transformation, Xi proposed initiatives including the BRICS initiative of AI-empowered new industrialization, the open source and inclusive AI initiative, the digital industry cooperation initiative, and the intelligent manufacturing cooperation initiative, Wang said. Third, Xi's visit guided China-India relations, Wang said. Xi and Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi conducted a candid and in-depth exchange of views on strategic, long-term and directional issues concerning China-India relations, Wang said, noting that the most important consensus they reached was that China and India should be partners. The Chinese president said China and India can draw on each other's strengths, support one another, help each other succeed and pursue common development, Wang said. The leaders of the two countries agreed to jointly maintain peace and tranquility in border areas, while the two countries will support each other as rotating chair of the BRICS, Wang said. ■

item.title: Xi, Modi conduct in-depth exchange of views, agree China, India should be partners
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-13
Chinese President Xi Jinping meets with Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi on the sidelines of the 18th BRICS Summit in New Delhi, India, Sept. 12, 2026. (Xinhua/Wang Ye) NEW DELHI, Sept. 12 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping and Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi conducted here on Saturday a candid and in-depth exchange of views, and reached important consensus that China and India should be partners. The two leaders met on the sidelines of the 18th BRICS Summit in New Delhi. Xi said China has always viewed and developed its relations with India from a strategic height and with a long-term perspective. Xi noted that he has met with Modi twice over the past two years, guiding bilateral relations from a new start to a further improvement. Institutional exchanges between the two countries have gradually resumed, the list of areas of cooperation has continued to grow, and bilateral trade has reached a new record high, Xi added. Xi said such hard-won progress should be cherished. Noting that China and India have different national conditions, Xi said they can draw on each other's strengths, support one another, help each other succeed and pursue common development. Amid a turbulent international landscape, China and India, as the world's two most populous countries and important members of the Global South, shoulder important responsibilities, Xi said. Xi called on the two sides to keep in mind the future of humanity and the well-being of peoples, work together to promote high-quality development of greater BRICS cooperation, and contribute more positive energy to world peace, stability, development and prosperity. Underscoring objective and rational strategic perception in calibrating China-India relations, Xi said China and India are partners for cooperation, not rivals. The two countries provide development opportunities for each other rather than pose threats to each other, he added. That is a strategic judgment based on the development stages of the two countries and the international environment, and serves the common interests of both countries and their peoples, Xi said. Xi called on both sides to help each other succeed through win-win cooperation. The two sides, Xi said, should focus on development as their greatest common denominator, while strengthening friendly exchanges and mutually beneficial cooperation. He called on the two sides to expand cooperation in people-to-people exchanges, direct flights and other areas to effectively strengthen the public support for bilateral relations. The two sides should also balance and address each other's economic and trade concerns, and promote a sound and stable development of bilateral economic and trade ties, Xi added. Xi called on China and India to draw on political wisdom of mutual respect and understanding to overcome disruptions, urging both sides to pursue parallel progress in bilateral ties and border issues with the two tracks reinforcing each other, so as to maintain peace and tranquility in border areas. He also urged China and India to promote multilateral cooperation with openness and inclusiveness to benefit the world. Xi said the two countries should support each other as rotating chair of the BRICS, strengthen coordination within such multilateral frameworks as the United Nations, the Shanghai Cooperation Organization and the Group of 20, stand together in addressing global challenges, and unequivocally uphold international fairness and justice. Modi said he has held several productive meetings with Xi, guiding India-China relations toward a positive direction, which serves the common interests of the more than 2.8 billion people of both countries. The two major civilizations of India and China have, over thousands of years, learned from each other through exchanges and moved forward hand in hand, he said. India always views India-China relations from a strategic height and a long-term perspective, and is willing to be a partner rather than a rival to China, and to regard each other's development as an opportunity rather than a challenge, he noted. India adheres to an independent foreign policy, and the development of its relations with China is not subject to the influence of any third party, he said. India's policy and position on the issues related to Taiwan and Xizang remain unchanged, and it does not allow any force to engage in anti-China activities in India, he said. India is ready to maintain high-level exchanges with China on the basis of mutual respect and mutual trust, strengthen strategic communication, promote mutually beneficial cooperation, and enhance people-to-people exchanges, so as to advance bilateral relations to greater heights, Modi said. The two sides should work together to safeguard peace and tranquility in the border areas, he added. India thanked China for its support for India's hosting of the BRICS summit and will fully support China in assuming the BRICS chairmanship next year, he said. Modi said India is ready to closely coordinate and cooperate with China to jointly strengthen cooperation among Global South countries, promote a more multipolar world and global economic growth, and serve as a force for stability and progress in a turbulent world. ■ Chinese President Xi Jinping meets with Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi on the sidelines of the 18th BRICS Summit in New Delhi, India, Sept. 12, 2026. (Xinhua/Yan Yan)

item.title: Xi urges BRICS to stand on right side of history, play pioneering role
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-13
* The BRICS cooperation mechanism has continued to grow and expand, and has demonstrated remarkable vitality and dynamism. * As to the future development of BRICS, Xi called on the grouping to pioneer in advancing innovation-driven development. NEW DELHI, Sept. 12 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping on Saturday urged BRICS countries to firmly stand on the right side of history and strive to be a pioneer of our times. When addressing the 18th BRICS Summit in New Delhi, Xi noted that this year marks the 20th anniversary of BRICS cooperation, saying the mechanism has become the world's most influential platform for cooperation among emerging markets and developing countries. Over the past two decades, BRICS has evolved into a broader platform for promoting shared growth, dialogue, and a greater representation of the Global South in international organizations, said analysts, noting that the group is expected to deliver more tangible results and foster a more balanced and inclusive world order in the future. TWO DECADES OF BRICS COOPERATION The BRICS cooperation mechanism was formally launched in 2006. The inaugural BRIC summit was convened in Yekaterinburg, Russia, in 2009. A year later, South Africa joined the grouping, turning BRIC into BRICS. Since then, the mechanism has continued to expand in both membership and areas of cooperation. Today, BRICS countries account for nearly half of the world's population, around 30 percent of the global economy and one-fifth of global trade, serving as a force for fostering a more representative and multipolar world and enhancing the voice of the Global South. Hailing the achievements over the past two decades, Xi said that the BRICS cooperation mechanism has continued to grow and expand, and has demonstrated remarkable vitality and dynamism. Elaborating on the 20-year history of the mechanism, Xi said it has been 20 years of self-reliance and self-strengthening, adding that BRICS countries have actively explored development paths suited to their own national conditions, setting an example of self-strengthening through unity among emerging markets and developing countries. The first decade of BRICS cooperation was primarily a period of institutional formation, and the second a period of expansion, said Rakhim Oshakbayev, director of the TALAP Center for Applied Research in Kazakhstan and former Kazakh vice minister for investment and development. But the significance of BRICS goes beyond the growth of its membership. Xi said that BRICS countries have established a comprehensive, multi-tiered framework for cooperation, and ushered in a new stage of high-quality development for greater BRICS cooperation. Rather than replacing existing global institutions, BRICS seeks to strengthen dialogue, equality, mutual respect and cooperation among nations, said Balew Demissie, a senior consultant at the Policy Studies Institute of Ethiopia. BRICS, with its expanded membership, provides a platform for emerging economies across the globe to have a stronger voice in global issues such as trade, development, finance, climate change, peace and security, Demissie said. PIONEERING ROLES As to the future development of BRICS, Xi called on the grouping to pioneer in advancing innovation-driven development. BRICS countries, he said, should strengthen cooperation in artificial intelligence and push practical cooperation into new areas and to new heights. China proposed an initiative to promote new industrialization through artificial intelligence among BRICS countries, and is willing to work with all parties to deliver more outcomes in research, development and application, and deepen cooperation in industrial and supply chains, he said. Oshakbayev said emerging technologies such as AI risk creating new technological divides between countries that possess advanced models, computing power and standard-setting capabilities and those that remain mainly users of technology. Joint research, research networks, education and training under BRICS could give developing countries greater opportunities to participate in technological innovation, he said. Xi also called on BRICS to be a pioneer in upholding peace and stability. Noting that the situation in the Middle East remains complex and fluid, Xi said this war has inflicted serious losses on the people of all countries in the region, and it is against the common interests of the international community. China will work with fellow BRICS members to play a due role in bringing peace and tranquility to the Middle East, he said. Diaa Helmy, founder and secretary-general of the Egyptian-Chinese Chamber of Commerce, said BRICS offers an important platform for cooperation rather than confrontation. "Within BRICS we do not compete; we complement one another," he said. On exchanges among civilizations, Xi called on BRICS countries to champion the common values of humanity and advocate exchanges and mutual learning among civilizations as well as harmonious coexistence. Such exchanges can help societies better understand one another while respecting differences, Oshakbayev said, adding that BRICS could contribute useful experience to dialogue among civilizations on an equal footing. Xi further called on BRICS to be a pioneer in reforming and improving global governance. He urged the group to keep pace with the trend toward greater democracy in international relations, promote a more just and equitable global governance system, and uphold the authority of the United Nations. Demissie, the expert from Ethiopia, said BRICS is not seeking to replace existing global institutions, but to make global governance more representative and responsive to the interests and aspirations of the Global South. BRICS RETURNS TO CHINA In his address, Xi announced that China will assume the rotating chair of BRICS and host the 19th BRICS Summit next year. During its previous chairmanships, China played a notable role in advancing the BRICS agendas. Over the past two decades, China has hosted three BRICS summits, each marking a new milestone in the group's evolution. When China hosted its first BRICS summit in the tropical resort of Sanya in 2011, South Africa attended the gathering as a new member for the first time. Six years later, in Xiamen, Xi proposed the "BRICS Plus" cooperation approach, inviting leaders from non-BRICS members to discuss international development cooperation and deepen South-South cooperation. When China chaired BRICS again in 2022, the leaders met virtually. China called for a "more comprehensive, close, practical and inclusive high-quality partnership" and emphasized global development. That summit laid the groundwork for the group's major expansion the following year. As BRICS cooperation enters its third "golden decade," a new chapter begins with China, with the Global South speaking with an even stronger voice. China is expected to work with other BRICS members to promote a more just and equitable global governance system by advocating multilateralism, greater representation for the Global South in financial and political institutions, said Farhana Paruk, a Cape Town-based China-Africa specialist. "I believe China's upcoming BRICS chairmanship could open a new phase that places greater emphasis on practical development and narrowing the gaps among the economies of member countries," said Salah El-Din Fahmy, professor of economics at Al-Azhar University in Egypt. "BRICS is still evolving," Fahmy said, noting that China can help advance this process gradually during its upcoming chairmanship by focusing on areas of common interest among member countries and promoting cooperation that makes the group more cohesive and better able to confront global challenges.■

item.title: Xi calls on BRICS to unite Global South, deepen cooperation
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-13
* The international landscape is volatile and fraught with risks and challenges, Xi said, adding that to bring stability to the world and make it a better place, BRICS countries must seize the historical initiative, rally the Global South, and advance the well-being of all humanity. * Xi proposed five initiatives on "greater BRICS" cooperation in areas of AI, trade and investment facilitation, digital industry, intelligent manufacturing, and science and technology talent development. NEW DELHI, Sept. 13 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping on Sunday called on BRICS countries to strengthen unity among the Global South and play an active, stabilizing and positive role in global affairs. In a speech when attending the second day of BRICS summit in New Delhi, Xi also outlined concrete proposals to further strengthen greater BRICS cooperation, with a focus on emerging areas including artificial intelligence, trade, digital industries and manufacturing. KEY DRIVER OF MULTIPOLARITY Xi pointed out that when changes unseen in a century are accelerating across the world, the Global South, with its collective rise, has become a key driver of world multipolarity. At the same time, the international landscape is volatile and fraught with risks and challenges, Xi said, adding that to bring stability to the world and make it a better place, BRICS countries must seize the historical initiative, rally the Global South, and advance the well-being of all humanity. Global South countries should jointly defend the rule of law in international affairs, safeguard the basic norms of international relations including sovereign equality, noninterference in internal affairs, and the peaceful settlement of disputes, Xi said. It should be ensured that international law and international rules are applied to all, and free from double standards, he added. Global South countries should hold high the banner of multilateralism, uphold the authority and role of the United Nations, and support multilateral institutions in advancing reform and increasing efficiency, Xi said. He also called for promoting the reform of the World Trade Organization in the right direction, as well as reforming and improving the international financial architecture to increase the representation and voice of developing countries. Global South countries should stay committed to a people-centered development philosophy and strive to deliver on the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development, Xi said. Global South countries should also jointly advance security governance, tackle both traditional and nontraditional security threats, and improve global climate governance, Xi said, also calling for working faster to evolve a consensus-based global AI governance framework, so that new technologies can light the way toward shared prosperity. "It is a solidarity that unlocks partnerships, unlocks democratization of the international system, unlocks an open international system, and unlocks an inclusive international system," said Charles Onunaiju, director of the Center for China Studies in Nigeria. Rakhim Oshakbayev, director of the TALAP Center for Applied Research in Kazakhstan and former Kazakh vice minister for investment and development, said BRICS cooperation should "bring together developing countries' shared aspirations and promote coordination and cooperation." BRICS countries should continue seeking common interests, he said, noting that the grouping's expansion had placed greater demands on internal coordination. GREATER BRICS COOPERATION During the speech, Xi proposed five initiatives on "greater BRICS" cooperation in areas of AI, trade and investment facilitation, digital industry, intelligent manufacturing, and science and technology talent development. To accomplish great things and achieve major progress, the foundation of greater BRICS cooperation must be cemented, Xi said, calling for leveraging BRICS' close ties with fellow emerging markets and Global South countries, upholding open cooperation for mutual benefit, safeguarding stable and smooth industrial and supply chains, and fostering a large integrated market. "We should build incubators for innovation, upgrade traditional industries, develop emerging industries, and deploy future industries," Xi said. On the open source and inclusive AI initiative, Xi said that China will be a pioneer in establishing a BRICS AI open source community, support the cooperation in developing and applying large language models, hold specialized AI seminars and training courses, and build an open ecosystem for AI. On the trade and investment facilitation initiative, China proposes to establish a BRICS special economic zone partnership, under which countries can set up an intelligent portal, coordinate policies, and build a new frontier for open development, Xi said, adding that in an effort to cultivate new drivers of economic and trade cooperation, China will hold the BRICS Forum on Trade in Services next year. On the digital industry cooperation initiative, Xi said that China will push for establishing a BRICS digital ecosystem cloud platform, and conduct digital skills training, technological exchange and industrial alignment, so as to jointly enable the development of the digital economy. On the intelligent manufacturing cooperation initiative, China stands ready to assist fellow BRICS countries in building smart factories and developing standards and norms, and jointly promote manufacturing transformation and upgrading, he said. On the science and technology talent development initiative, China proposes to set up a BRICS engineer cultivation alliance for joint development of engineers and mutual recognition of competency standards, Xi said, adding that China will launch a BRICS youth exchange program for scientific and technological innovation, so as to cultivate more high-caliber talent. The five initiatives proposed by Xi focus on key areas including technology, industry, trade and talent, providing concrete pathways to lay a solid foundation for practical cooperation among the broader BRICS community, said Serik Korzhumbayev, editor-in-chief of the Delovoy Kazakhstan newspaper. It demonstrates China's firm resolve to share the opportunities of its modernization, a reflection of the spirit of openness, inclusiveness and mutual benefit that underpins BRICS cooperation, he said.■
